title: Refined separation of combined Fe–Hf from rock matrices for isotope analyses using AG-MP-1M and Ln-Spec chromatographic extraction resins
author: Cheng, Nebel, et al.

steps.title: Prepare distilled acids and rock
steps.instruction: Purify all HF, HCl, and HNO₃ by sub‑boiling distillation; weigh the required amount of rock powder.

steps.title: Dissolve rock in acid mixture
steps.instruction: Add 2–3 mL 15.7 M HNO₃ to 24 M HF in a 1 : 2.2 ratio (total 5 mL) in Teflon vials and heat: 150 °C on a hotplate for 24 h, or for zircon/chromite samples place vials in steel‑jacketed Teflon bombs and heat in an oven at 200 °C for 48 h.

steps.title: Break fluoride bonds
steps.instruction: After complete evaporation of the acids, add several drops of concentrated HNO₃ and one drop of a 0.5 M HCl + 0.5 M HF mixed acid; repeat if necessary to dissolve CaF complexes.

steps.title: Transfer to 9 M HCl
steps.instruction: Take up the residue in 9 M HCl, store the vials on the hotplate overnight, then centrifuge to remove any microscopic residues and pipette the clear supernatant onto the chromatography resin.

steps.title: Prepare AG‑MP‑1M column
steps.instruction: Pack 1 mL AG‑MP‑1M cation resin into a modified polyethylene syringe (≈10 cm length, 0.5 cm internal diameter) equipped with a bottom frit and a 5‑mL pipette‑tip acid reservoir; condition the column as described in the method.

steps.title: Separate Fe from matrix
steps.instruction: Load the 9 M HCl sample onto the AG‑MP‑1M column; elute the matrix with 9 M HCl (collect for later Hf/Lu purification), rinse with 5 M HCl, elute semi‑ and transitional metals, then elute Fe with 1 M HCl, evaporate the Fe fraction to dryness for isotope analysis.

steps.title: Dilute Hf/Lu fraction
steps.instruction: Dilute the collected 9 M HCl matrix fraction to 6 M HCl if only Hf is required, or to 3 M HCl if both Lu and Hf are needed, ensuring the acid concentration does not exceed the elution scheme limits.

steps.title: Load LN‑Spec column
steps.instruction: Load the diluted Hf/Lu solution onto a 1 mL LN‑Spec resin column (prepared in a similar syringe format).

steps.title: Optional load concentration step
steps.instruction: If a smaller acid load is desired, evaporate the diluted solution to dryness and re‑dissolve in the appropriate acid before loading onto the LN‑Spec column.

steps.title: Elute Ti (if needed)
steps.instruction: Elute titanium using a mixture of 0.09 M citric acid, 0.40 M HNO₃ and 1 % H₂O₂ as described by Münker et al.

steps.title: Elute Hf (and Zr)
steps.instruction: Elute Hf (and co‑eluted Zr) from the LN‑Spec column with 0.5 M HF, gently evaporate to dryness, and re‑dissolve the residue in 1 mL of 0.54 M HNO₃ + 0.24 M HF mixed acid for mass‑spectrometric analysis.

description: We combined two individual separation techniques to purify Fe and Hf from rock matrices for subsequent isotope analyses using mass spectrometry from a single dissolution batch. Iron is particularly problematic due to its incomplete separation from Hf, which can cause isobaric interferences (matrix effects) during Hf isotope mass-spectrometric measurements [1–4]. We present a combined and refined version of a “clean-up” step initially designed to remove Fe that is required for Hf purification. Using this method facilitates the collection and subsequent analyses of both elements from a single rock matrix. The procedure follows the steps:1.Rock powder is dissolved in a concentrated acid mixture of 24 M HF–15.7 M HNO3 in a ratio of 1:2.2.Sample treatment with concentrated HNO3 after evaporation breaks down fluoride (as e.g., CaF) bonds that form during the chemical dissolution.3.Final uptake in strong (9 M) HCl ensures the full dissolution of sample material and the formation of (iron) chloro-compounds.4.Samples are first passed through Bio-Rad AG-MP-1M cation resin in steps of 9-5-1M HCl, separating Fe (1 M) from the rock matrix (9 + 5 M)5.Subsequently Hf (and possibly Lu for old samples that require age correction) is separated from the 9 M HCl matrix fraction (after diluting it) using Eichrom Ln-Spec.
